text:
Nikita Kucherov asked the Lightning for a trade around Halloween, and said publicly that it came from what he called disrespect and a lack of communication. Then he went out and put up 16 points in his next ten games. The reigning Hart Trophy winner has 31 points (9 goals, 22 assists) in 22 games and played his 900th NHL game against Washington on Nov. 17, all in a Tampa Bay sweater.

The play behind it is as good as ever. Tampa Bay controls 60.8% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at 5v5 with him on the ice, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 10.6 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 96th percentile among forwards. Evolving-Hockey rated him the second-most valuable forward in the league in 2025-26.

One caution: his teammates have scored 9.0 more goals than their chances deserve with him out there, which pads the assist column. His own scoring rate actually sits a touch below our talent estimate (4.02 points per 60 against 4.4), so our season range of 111 to 145 points holds up even if the bounces cool. The bigger question is which sweater he wears for them.
